scope: six old-candidate boundary modules and two probes only; not whole-candidate approval

blockers.issue: Connection-wait authorization disclosure is real and unfixed in this source: in post() (lines 272-295) request.reauthorize() runs BEFORE client.send(), and client.send() performs DNS/TCP/TLS establishment and pool waits internally. Any expiry/revocation that lands during that connection wait is never observed before the private request body (including the count request, which carries the full serialized input) is written to the socket. There is no httpcore trace gate at send_request_headers/body as in card_transport.py. The module docstring (lines 27-31) promises authorization after blocking work with only clock/cancel checks afterward, but the connection wait sits between authorization and body egress.
blockers.reproduction: parent_real_tls_egress.py --expect-old-gap (supplied stdout parent-real-tls-old-red.stdout): TLSBarrier holds after a real loopback TLS handshake and before any HTTP bytes; revoked[0]/now[0] are flipped during the hold; the private body is still sent (private_body_sent=true in expiry and revocation modes, authorization_samples showing the reauthorize decision preceded the wait). I did not run this; the stdout is supplied evidence, and the static ordering in post() confirms the window. Minimum fix: add a synchronous trace hook gating at 'http11.send_request_headers.started' and 'http11.send_request_body.started' that re-runs request.reauthorize() + check() (reauthorize is already synchronous, so no await-after-authorize violation), mapping failures through the existing _authorization_reason sanitizer, with a one-shot-per-request latch. Verify by re-running the same probe without --expect-old-gap: expiry/revocation modes must show private_body_sent=false and a post-TLS authorization sample observing the denied state.

blockers.issue: ACK acceptance re-checks credentials in the wrong order relative to retention I/O. acceptance_policy() (lines 356-358) calls transport.check_ack(attempt, ack) FIRST and policy() SECOND. policy() -> _current() -> retention check_guard performs a bounded retention-ledger SQLite read (real writer wait, 50ms). A credential rotation committed during that retention wait lands AFTER the credential digest revalidation and BEFORE commit, so a stale-credential CardCreateAck is still committed with state='create_acknowledged' — the exact 'ACK token rotation during retention I/O' gap the probe targets. Additionally the probe's fixed-code expectation tokens==0 is not implied by these modules: card_tokens rows are created at prepare() and nothing on the acknowledge-failure path deletes them (they are only fenced by _navigate's state=='create_acknowledged' check). Either prune card_tokens when acknowledgment fails, or correct the probe's assertion; the state fence already neutralizes stale tokens, so this must be an explicit, documented choice.
blockers.reproduction: parent_ack_credentials.py rotate mode: race.arm() fires at ledger.acknowledge entry; if RetentionContention's change() (access_token rotation via the patched _resolve) lands during the retention read inside policy(), check_ack has already succeeded and the ACK commits despite rotation. Static confirmation: lines 357-358 ordering. Minimum fix: reorder acceptance_policy to run policy() (retention + mirror) first and self.transport.check_ack(attempt, ack) as the final local check before _clock_live/commit, matching retention.py's documented lock order (retention read -> original mirror -> final fence). Verify: rotate mode must yield state='unknown'; valid mode must still commit; and a new variant rotating during the retention wait specifically (not before acknowledge entry) must also yield 'unknown'.

blockers.issue: Analogous text-transport boundary is strictly weaker than the card boundary. (a) The 'http11.send_request_body.started' trace branch (lines 233-235) re-resolves the credential snapshot but does NOT re-invoke before_egress, so a retention revoke/cancellation committed during the awaited header write is invisible before the private body is sent — the precise window card_transport.py closes with its second gate call (card lines 159-166). delivery.py's egress() is single-use (egress_used latch), so the transport cannot add the second call without a coordinated change. (b) The U01 acceptance path (delivery.py accept_delivery_response with precommit=policy) has no post-I/O credential-digest revalidation analogous to CardTransport.check_ack; it relies entirely on the authorize mirror and binding.generation, so a token rotation that does not bump generation is undetectable at acceptance.
blockers.reproduction: Static: compare feishu_transport.py lines 230-235 (body branch: check()+snapshot only) with card_transport.py lines 155-166 (body branch re-runs the full gate); and delivery.py lines 173-198 (single-shot egress) plus lines 238-240 (accept with policy only, no credential digest). Minimum fix: make delivery.py's egress gate exactly two-shot (mirroring card's used<2), have the feishu body trace branch re-invoke before_egress, and document or close the acceptance-side digest asymmetry (at minimum, assert by contract test that any CredentialSnapshot change bumps binding.generation, or add a check_ack-equivalent before accept_delivery_response commits). Verify: a probe that revokes retention between header-write start and body-write start on the text path must produce no private body on the wire.

notes: Scope: this review covers only the six boundary modules and the two supplied probes. No whole-candidate or A10 approval is expressed or implied. I did not execute any test, compute any hash, or inspect files outside the supplied list; the two .stdout files are treated as supplied evidence, not independently reproduced results.

Probe 1 (parent_real_tls_egress) is structurally valid red evidence of the OLD openai connection-wait disclosure: the barrier interposes after a real TLS handshake and before HTTP bytes, and the revocation-mode sample (9,true) shows the second reauthorize fired only after the first private body had already leaked via the count request. Caveats: it patches private httpcore internals (wire._pool._network_backend, AutoBackend.connect_tcp), making it version-fragile; it gates only the first connection's TLS; and it exercises logical (mock-clock) expiry, not the monotonic deadline — acceptable for the authority boundary. It doubles as the correct fix verification when run without --expect-old-gap.

Probe 2 (parent_ack_credentials) is INCONCLUSIVE as supplied: its correctness depends on unsupplied helpers (test_brief_retention.full_stack, test_brief_revocation.RetentionContention, test_brief_service.SCOPE) whose interleaving semantics — exactly when change() fires relative to check_ack, policy()'s retention read, and COMMIT — cannot be audited here. Those helpers must be disclosed for the probe to be evidence. As noted in blocker 2, its new-code tokens==0 expectation is also unsupported by the supplied modules.

Realistic boundary vs impossible revocation: retention.py's framing (lines 46-61) is correct and should be retained — a revocation committed after the final durable fence, bytes already handed to kernel/TLS, and another coordinator/process's unpinned mutation cannot be retracted or observed until the next durable check; remote cards persist (remote_cards_may_persist=True). I do not demand elimination of OS scheduling or remote atomic recall. The achievable and required boundary is: last durable authorization + credential revalidation placed as the final local operations before the body-write syscall and before COMMIT, which is exactly what the current openai/card/feishu orderings fail to do.

Smaller observations (not independently blocking): openai_transport.py line 320 compares token count n against budget.max_input_bytes (token/byte conflation — conservative direction, but clarify); feishu_transport.py line 323 re-raises the original gate_error across cleanup while card_transport.py line 252 sanitizes to _fail() — currently safe only because delivery.py's egress raises fixed DeliveryError codes, so this contract should be asserted; card_transport.py bounds response headers (line 202-204) while feishu_transport.py does not; _ack's requirement that create responses carry deleted/updated == False should be verified against the pinned Feishu create schema during integration certification.
